title: Houston VA Emergency Room Expansion
scope: Complete ground truth for all twelve supplied Houston VA Emergency Room Expansion mechanical sheets: title-block/project/sheet review; all 69 rows and 778 cells in MH601's seven schedules; all 19 MH502 VAV point-matrix rows; written VAV and isolation-room sequences; explicit schedule-to-point-template boundary; and manual-ball-valve/air-device/filter classification limits. No unprinted installed I/O total, controller terminal count, BAS protocol, network topology, valve actuator/Cv/fail position, damper-actuator schedule, or point-matrix-to-equipment multiplier is invented.
reading_notes: All twelve supplied pages were reviewed as full-page 180 DPI Poppler renders. MuPDF and Poppler independently corroborate every authored schedule/points cell and bounded text assertion.

MH601 has seven populated schedules and 69 source rows: 20 single-duct terminals, 1 series fan-powered terminal, 8 air-device type rows, 2 filter rows, and 38 heating-hot-water supply/return BALL VALVE rows.

The 38 valve rows are literal tagged manual ball valves with service, size and flow. Because the schedule has no actuator, Cv, control signal or fail position, they are deliberately excluded from BAS control-valve/actuator counts.

MH502's 19-row VAV terminal unit point list is a printed point-function matrix with no terminal equipment-tag column or source binding to MH601 schedule rows. Its listed hardware/software totals are not multiplied into installed I/O or controller-terminal totals.

MH502 nevertheless contains high-value written behavior: continuous VAV operation, occupied/unoccupied airflow and reheat logic, discharge-temperature/humidity alarms, and isolation-room differential-pressure, HEPA-filter, lead/standby-fan, VFD and fan-alarm sequences.

requirement_audit.finding: Project title, Houston site, VA project number, building number and date are captured from the repeated title block; blank revision-log structure is not treated as a revision event.
Every supplied page has exact title and sheet-number witnesses plus a full-page visual finding.
The repeated title block has no document-wide scale field. Geometric takeoff must read each view's local scale and no universal conversion is inferred.

Twenty-one terminal marks are retained as scheduled terminal identities. Air-device rows, filter service rows and the 38 manual-ball-valve tags remain separately classified rather than converted into BAS equipment/actuator quantities.
All 778 source cells of the 69 populated MH601 schedule rows are retained, including terminal airflows/coils, air-device fields, filters and ball-valve service/size/flow.

Nineteen exact MH502 VAV matrix rows are retained. The source supplies neither terminal tags in that matrix nor row-level controller/wiring/ownership; zero unprinted instance applications are emitted.
No BAS vendor, protocol, transport, controller/panel model, address or topology is stated in the supplied twelve sheets.
VAV operation and isolation-room pressure/filter/fan sequences are captured from MH502. The source does not state that the point template applies to every MH601 terminal.
Temperature, airflow, humidity, pressure and filter-pressure roles appear in MH502, but no installed sensor schedule or plan-mapped physical sensor count is stated.
Manual ball-valve rows are not recast as BAS control valves, the point matrix is unexpanded, and air-device/filter source rows are not silently made into plan quantities.
All twelve supplied pages were reviewed at full-page resolution; saved Poppler renders and page dispositions are embedded and hash-checked.
Bundle build and validation rerun every authored module against retained MuPDF and Poppler captures, then record current source/manifest/module digests.

controls_context.module_role: MH502 controls ground truth. It preserves the printed VAV and isolation-room sequences alongside the MH502 template point matrix without manufacturing controller instances, wiring counts, or network details.

control_valve_schedule.basis: MH502 prints an AO reheat-valve schematic/sequence, and MH601 prints 38 heating-hot-water BALL VALVE rows. Neither sheet prints a control-valve schedule with actuator, Cv, control signal, or fail-position fields.

damper_actuator_schedule.basis: MH502 depicts an AO zone damper and sequence behavior, but the supplied set contains no damper-actuator schedule.

physical_schedule_line_item_count.basis: The only printed valve rows are the MH601 manual-ball-valve schedule, which is retained separately and not recast as a BAS control-valve schedule.

point_matrix_context.interpretation_rule: The MH502 VAV terminal-unit list is a point-function template. It is not row-mapped to the 20 MH601 single-duct terminal rows or TU26-73, so printed matrix totals are not expanded into project-wide physical I/O totals.
source_roles: AO zone damper and AO reheating valve
occupied/unoccupied airflow setpoints and heating mode
zone humidity/humidity setpoint and high humidity alarm

sequences.source_behavior: The unit runs continuously, maintaining 75°F adjustable cooling and 70°F adjustable heating setpoints; occupants can adjust the zone temperature heating and cooling setpoints at the zone sensor.

Above cooling setpoint, the zone damper modulates between minimum occupied airflow and maximum cooling airflow until satisfied. Between cooling and heating setpoints it maintains minimum required zone airflow. Below heating setpoint it modulates the heating valve open; if warm AHU air is available it also modulates the zone damper between minimum occupied and maximum heating airflow until satisfied.

The zone damper controls to minimum unoccupied airflow. Above cooling setpoint it modulates to maximum cooling airflow; below unoccupied heating setpoint the controller modulates the heating valve open and, if warm AHU air is available, modulates the damper between minimum unoccupied airflow and auxiliary heating airflow until satisfied.

The controller measures discharge-air temperature and limits hot-water valve position when discharge air is more than 15°F adjustable above zone temperature. High discharge temperature is greater than 100°F adjustable; low is less than 50°F adjustable. A space relative-humidity value above 60% initiates a visible alarm in the affected OR and at the DDC monitoring station.

The DDC system modulates the exhaust-air venturi valve to maintain +0.01 inches water gauge to the corridor, opening below that value for more than five seconds and closing above it for more than five seconds. Low differential pressure below 0.00 inches for more than 15 seconds causes a local visual alarm and DDC-monitoring-station alarm.

sequences.scope: Isolation room HEPA pre-filter and HEPA filter
sequences.source_behavior: The DDC system monitors differential pressure across the HEPA pre-filter and HEPA filter; alarms occur above 1.0 inches water gauge for the pre-filter and 2.0 inches water gauge for the HEPA filter. The HEPA filter also receives a visual Magnehelic gauge.

The two fans operate lead/standby. The lead runs first with the standby isolation damper closed; on lead failure, the standby runs with the lead isolation damper closed. Lead rotation is user-selectable manually, by adjustable runtime, weekly, or monthly. VFD output modulates from duct static pressure ahead of the filter, with the setpoint determined during TAB.
Alarms include failure when commanded on but status is off, running in hand when commanded off but status is on, and runtime exceeded when status runtime exceeds a user-definable limit.

sensor_and_zone_ledger.source_typed_roles: MH502 prints temperature, airflow, humidity, space-pressure, and filter-pressure roles in a VAV point template, sequences, and an isolation-room schematic. It does not provide an installed sensor schedule or plan-mapped physical sensor count.
sensor_and_zone_ledger.written_visual_indicator: The isolation-room sequence calls for a ball-thru-wall manual pressure differential indicator between the ante room and corridor; this is not counted as a BAS point or sensor instance.

source_limitations: No BAS vendor, protocol, controller/panel model, address, transport, or network topology is printed in the supplied 12-page set.
No MH502 control-sequence statement identifies which, if any, of the twenty MH601 single-duct terminal schedule rows are the represented VAV template instances.
MH601's valve table provides plain ball-valve service/size/flow rows only; it cannot supply actuator, fail-position, Cv, or BAS control-valve takeoff fields.

assertions.expected: RUN CONDITIONS - CONTINUOUS: THE UNIT SHALL RUN CONTINUOUSLY AND SHALL MAINTAIN: • A 75°F (ADJ.) COOLING SETPOINT. • A 70°F (ADJ.) HEATING SETPOINT.
THE OCCUPANT SHALL BE ABLE TO ADJUST THE ZONE TEMPERATURE HEATING AND COOLING SETPOINTS AT THE ZONE SENSOR.

WHEN ZONE TEMPERATURE IS GREATER THAN ITS COOLING SETPOINT, THE ZONE DAMPER SHALL MODULATE BETWEEN THE MINIMUM OCCUPIED AIRFLOW (ADJ.) AND THE MAXIMUM COOLING AIRFLOW (ADJ.) UNTIL THE ZONE IS SATISFIED.
WHEN THE ZONE IS UNOCCUPIED THE ZONE DAMPER SHALL CONTROL TO ITS MINIMUM UNOCCUPIED AIRFLOW (ADJ.).
THE CONTROLLER SHALL MEASURE THE DISCHARGE AIR TEMPERATURE AND LIMIT HOT WATER VALVE POSITION IF THE DISCHARGE AIR TEMPERATURE IS MORE THAN 15°F (ADJ.) ABOVE THE ZONE TEMPERATURE.
HIGH DISCHARGE AIR TEMP: IF THE DISCHARGE AIR TEMPERATURE IS GREATER THAN 100°F (ADJ.).
HIGH HUMIDITY: IF THE SPACE RELATIVE HUMIDITY RISES ABOVE 60% A VISIBLE ALARM SHALL BE INITIATED IN THE AFFECTED OR AND AT THE DDC MONITORING STATION.
THE DDC SYSTEM SHALL MODULATE THE EXHAUST AIR VENTURI VALVE TO MAINTAIN A SET POINT OF +0.01 INCHES WATER GAUGE TO THE CORRIDOR.
LOW DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE IF THE PRESSURE FALLS BELOW 0.00 INCHES FOR MORE THAN 15 SECONDS. A LOCAL VISUAL ALARM SHALL BE INDICATED AND AN ALARM SHALL BE ANNUNCIATED AT THE DDC MONITORING STATION.
THE DDC SYSTEM SHALL MONITOR THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE ACROSS THE HEPA PRE-FILTER AND THE HEPA FILTER. THE HEPA FILTER SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH A VISUAL MANGEHELIC GAUGE AS WELL.

FAN CONTROL: THE TWO FANS SHALL OPERATE IN A LEAD / STANDBY FASHION. • THE LEAD FAN SHALL RUN FIRST AND THE STANDBY FAN ISOLATION DAMPER SHALL BE CLOSED. • ON FAILURE OF THE LEAD FAN, THE STANDBY FAN SHALL RUN AND THE LEAD FAN ISOLATION DAMPER SHALL BE CLOSED.
UPON A FALL IN DUCT STATIC PRESSURE AHEAD OF THE FILTER AT A SET POINT AS DETERMINED DURING TAB, THE VFD SHALL MODULATE UP. ON A RISE THE VFD SHALL MODULATE DOWN.

ALARMS TO BOTH FANS SHALL BE PROVIDED AS FOLLOWS: • FAILURE: COMMANDED ON, BUT THE STATUS IS OFF. • RUNNING IN HAND: COMMANDED OFF, BUT THE STATUS IS ON. • RUNTIME EXCEEDED: STATUS RUN TIME EXCEEDS A USER DEFINABLE LIMIT.

plan_and_detail_reconciliation.finding: Twenty single-duct and one series fan-powered terminal marks are literal schedule identities. Multi-room cells remain literal source cells and are not expanded into per-room terminal counts.
EG, RG and SD rows are air-device types/ranges, not plan-counted installed outlet instances; they remain schedule-row type identities.
The two filter rows both print ROOF location with no distinct equipment mark, so they are retained as source service/type rows rather than forced into duplicate physical identity keys.

All 38 valve rows print BALL VALVE with heating-hot-water supply/return service, size and flow. The source does not print Cv, actuator, control signal or fail position, so they are retained as manual ball-valve tags and excluded from BAS control-valve/actuator quantities.

control_valve_schedule.note: MH601 has a populated 38-row manual BALL VALVE schedule. It has no actuator, Cv, BAS signal, or fail-position fields, so it is not recast as a BAS control-valve schedule.

damper_actuator_schedule.note: Air-device schedule rows state damper/damper-diffuser properties but no damper actuator schedule, actuator model, torque, signal or fail position is printed.

point_applications.module_role: Unexpanded printed-matrix ledger. MH502's VAV terminal unit point list has point-name and flag columns but no equipment-instance tag column or source rule binding the template to the twenty MH601 VAV schedule rows or the one series fan-powered row.
point_applications.source_points_composite: points_mh502 holds the 19 printed VAV terminal point-function rows, including hardware/software flag columns and source totals.
point_applications.ownership_binding_semantics: The points matrix does not print field equipment tags, controller identities, I/O terminal ownership, wiring method or protocol. Written sequences identify DDC behavior but do not create row-level installed-point assignments.
point_applications.expanded_count_warning: Nineteen is the number of printed source matrix rows. Zero is intentionally the number of emitted instance applications: no multiplier from the schedule is source-stated, so no field I/O or controller-terminal count is manufactured.

installed_IO_total.reason: No installed equipment-instance point matrix, controller schedule, panel terminal list, network point export, or source multiplier is supplied.

point_transport.note: No protocol or transport is assigned to individual MH502 matrix rows.

supporting_evidence.module_role: Supporting full-set evidence and source limitations qualifying use of the MH502 point matrix and MH601 schedules for BAS takeoff.
source_limitations: MH502's 19 VAV terminal point-function rows have no terminal-equipment tag column and no printed rule applying them to the twenty MH601 VAV rows or TU26-73. They remain an unexpanded source template.
The supplied twelve-sheet set prints no BAS vendor, network protocol, controller/panel model, addressing, transport or point-to-controller terminal schedule.
MH601's populated VALVE SCHEDULE contains 38 heating-hot-water supply/return BALL VALVE rows. It does not print control-valve Cv, actuator, control signal or fail position.
The printed air-device rows are type/range schedules, and the two filter rows have no distinct equipment mark. Neither is treated as an installed plan quantity without an explicit source binding.
